head: No key.
Nothing wrong.
That's the bug.
body: I found a chat list in my own app that identifies rows by position.
It works. I wanted to know why.

head: The Recomposer,
*waiting
slides.caption: Not redrawing anything today. He's waiting for the list to reorder, and for a row to remember something.

head: Position-keyed,
with an id in hand
callout: It's safe for two lucky reasons.
The chat only appends, and the row holds no remembered state.

head: The id is a
timestamp
body: The id is "u_" or "a_" plus a millisecond timestamp. Two messages from one side in the same millisecond would collide.
A keyed list throws on a duplicate key. Add the key and you inherit a crash that was always latent.

head: Key it when you
write the list.
*Then check the id.
body: A missing key stays invisible while rows are stateless and the list only grows.
That's exactly why it survives review.
